Simple: interest on principal only. Compound: interest on interest too. ₩10M @ 5% for 10 years: simple ₩15M, monthly compound ~₩16.48M.

faq.q: Can rates vary year by year?

world-time.description: See current time in Seoul, Tokyo, New York, London, Paris, Sydney, and more major cities at once. Add/remove cities with real-time updates. Useful for travel and overseas business trips, scheduling video meetings, calling friends/family abroad, and global collaboration.
world-time.metaDescription: Free world clock. Per-city current time, real-time updates.

Departure time + flight duration = arrival in departure timezone. Then convert to destination. Pair with [Time Calculator].

name-picker.description: Randomly pick N items from a list. Great for choosing dinner spots, selecting presenters, draw winners, forming class/club teams, and ordering game turns. Powered by Web Crypto for genuinely random, fair results.

caffeine.description: Add up today's caffeine from coffee, tea, and energy drinks, and compare against the 400mg adult daily limit. Useful for cutting back on coffee, gauging dependence, monitoring safe pregnancy intake, and analyzing sleep impact.

chinese-zodiac.metaDescription: Free Chinese zodiac. 12 animals with stem-branch (60-jiazi), lunar Ipchun basis.

faq.a: Traditionally, zodiac follows lunar Ipchun (early February), so Jan–Feb births may belong to the previous year's sign. Saju uses Ipchun; everyday usage often uses Jan 1.

faq.q: What is the order of the 12 animals?
faq.a: Rat (자), Ox (축), Tiger (인), Rabbit (묘), Dragon (진), Snake (사), Horse (오), Goat (미), Monkey (신), Rooster (유), Dog (술), Pig (해).
10 stems × 12 branches combine in a 60-year cycle. Names like '경자년' or '갑오년' come from this.

faq.q: Same zodiac in Korea, China, Japan?
faq.a: Nearly the same, with small differences. Japan's 'rabbit' is sometimes 'wild boar'; Vietnam uses 'cat' instead of 'rabbit'.
Enter the current year — 2026 is Horse, 2027 is Goat (by Ipchun).

alcohol-converter.description: Convert alcohol amounts across drink types — soju, beer, wine, whiskey, and more — for equivalent comparison. Useful for gauging your limit at hweshik, calculating sober-up time, and comparing drinks.
alcohol-converter.metaDescription: Free alcohol converter. Soju ↔ beer ↔ wine, strength and total volume.
howTo: Pick a reference drink and number of glasses.

faq.a: Korea's legal limit is BAC 0.03%. Even one drink (a shot of soju or 200ml beer) is risky — don't drink and drive.

faq.q: Same alcohol in a shot of soju and a glass of beer?
faq.a: Soju 50ml at 17% ≈ 8.5g alcohol. Beer 200ml at 5% ≈ 10g. Roughly equal. A 500ml draft = about 3 shots of soju.
Adult males metabolize ~0.015% BAC per hour. From 0.05%, ~3 hours to 0%. Varies by person and whether you ate.

faq.q: Bottle of wine = how much soju?
faq.a: Wine 750ml at 12% ≈ 90g alcohol. Soju bottle (360ml, 17%) ≈ 60g. One wine bottle ≈ 1.5 soju bottles.
Supports makgeolli (6%), cheongju (15%), sake (15%), whiskey (40%), vodka (40%), and other major types.
Rough estimates by body weight and gender are possible, but a breathalyzer is the only accurate measure. Never drink and drive.

bmr.description: Calculate BMR and activity-adjusted TDEE from gender, age, height, and weight — your baseline calories for cutting or bulking. Useful for meal planning, exercise dosing, and diagnosing weight plateaus.
bmr.metaDescription: Free BMR/TDEE calculator. Mifflin-St Jeor formula, activity-adjusted.

faq.a: Mifflin-St Jeor — considered the most accurate modern formula, 5–10% more accurate than Harris-Benedict.
BMR = minimum energy at rest. TDEE = BMR + activity/exercise. For dieting, target TDEE.

faq.q: How do I pick an activity level?
faq.a: Sedentary (BMR×1.2), light exercise 1–3×/wk (×1.375), moderate 3–5× (×1.55), active 6–7× (×1.725), very active (×1.9).
TDEE − 500 kcal gives about 0.5 kg/week loss. −1000 is 1 kg/week, but too steep risks muscle loss and rebound.

faq.q: Is there a more accurate formula for muscular people?
faq.a: Katch-McArdle (uses body fat %) is more accurate. If you know your body fat % (InBody), use that instead.

faq.q: Will I lose weight just following these numbers?
faq.a: BMR is an estimate (±5%) and actual burn varies by daily routine, sleep, and stress. Adjust after observing 2–3 weeks of progress.

running-pace.description: Enter any two of distance, time, or pace to get the third. Includes finish time predictions for 5K, 10K, half, and full marathon.
running-pace.metaDescription: Free running pace calculator. Min/km, 5K/10K/marathon time prediction.
howTo: Enter any two of distance, time, or pace.

faq.q: How accurate are the marathon predictions?
faq.a: Based on the Riegel formula, which estimates marathon time from your 5K pace. Real-world pace can be slightly slower, especially after 30km.
The time it takes to run 1km (min:sec). '5:30/km' means 5 minutes 30 seconds per kilometer. Lower is faster.
When you're starting out, 6:30~7:30/km is reasonable. Running long and slow comes first; speed builds gradually.
Finishing a full marathon in under 3 or 4 hours. Sub-4 needs about 5:41/km; sub-3 needs about 4:15/km sustained.
Treadmills have no wind resistance and the belt assists you, making you about 0.5~1 min/km faster than outdoors. Adjust accordingly.

faq.q: Can I calculate without a GPS watch?
faq.a: Just knowing your distance (one track lap = 400m) and time is enough. Many running courses publish distance markers — check yours.

tip-calculator.description: Enter bill total, tip rate, and party size to get per-person share. For US/EU restaurants.
tip-calculator.metaDescription: Free tip calculator. Rate, party size, split evenly — for US and EU dining.
howTo: Enter the bill total and tip rate (usually 15~20%).

faq.q: Do I use tips in Korea?
faq.a: Korea generally doesn't have tipping culture. Only hotel restaurants with included service charges sometimes get extra. Mostly used when traveling abroad.

faq.q: What's the standard tip rate in US restaurants?
faq.a: Casual dining 15~20%, fine dining 20~25%, delivery 10~15%. Give more for great service.
Italy, France etc. often include service charges, so 5~10% extra is plenty. UK around 12.5%. Germany 5~10%.
In the US, 10~15% is typical. Uber lets you add tip in the app. Korea doesn't tip.

faq.q: Is it rude to skip the tip?
faq.a: Very rude in the US. Unless service is truly terrible, give at least 10~15%. Europe is more relaxed.

faq.q: How to enter tip when paying by card?
faq.a: Write the amount in the 'Tip' line on the receipt and add up the total. Some terminals let you pick a percentage on screen.

unit-price.description: Compare prices of two products of different sizes per unit (100ml, 100g, etc.) to see which is cheaper.
unit-price.metaDescription: Free unit price compare. See which size of two products is cheaper.
howTo: Enter price and size for both products.
It instantly shows which is cheaper.
Also shows the per-unit price difference.

faq.a: Any unit — ml, L, g, kg, count, etc. The tool automatically converts to the same unit for comparison.

faq.q: Why do supermarkets show price per 100g?
faq.a: Many countries require unit pricing (per 100g, per 100ml, etc.) for processed food and household goods. Check the small print on the price tag.
Usually, but marketing or stock clearance can make small sizes cheaper. Always compare per-unit price.
Just enter the final price after discount. For BOGO, it's two items for one price, so divide by 2.

faq.q: Should I buy big if shelf life is short?
faq.a: Don't just look at price — consider how fast you'll use it. Throwing food away makes 'cheap' expensive.
Yes. Especially helpful for comparing different sizes or sellers of the same item.

dice-coin.description: Roll various dice (D4, D6, D8, D10, D12, D20, D100) and flip coins. For board games, TRPGs, and decisions.
dice-coin.metaDescription: Free dice and coin tool. D4 to D100, secure Web Crypto random.
howTo: Pick the die type (sides) and number of dice.
Roll again as many times as you want.

faq.a: Uses Web Crypto's cryptographically secure random. More statistically uniform than Math.random().
A 20-sided die. Most commonly used in TRPGs like Dungeons & Dragons. 1 is a critical fail, 20 is a critical hit.

faq.q: Can I roll multiple at once?
faq.a: Yes. Specify count like '3D6' (three 6-sided dice) to see the sum and each result together.
Statistically nearly uniform. Short trials may lean one way due to randomness, but it averages out.
Fine for fun. For important decisions, weigh pros and cons rather than relying on pure random.
Statistically the same. Physical dice aren't perfectly balanced either, so digital is arguably more reliable for randomness.

rps.description: Play rock paper scissors against the computer. Win rate stats included.
rps.metaDescription: Free rock paper scissors. Play the computer, win rate tracked.
howTo: Play multiple rounds and see your cumulative win rate.

faq.a: Fully fair random. Doesn't learn your patterns. Uses Web Crypto random.

faq.q: Why is rock paper scissors fair?
faq.a: Each choice is exactly 1/3 probability. Scissors beats paper, paper beats rock, rock beats scissors — a cycle with no superior option.

faq.q: Are there patterns like with humans?
faq.a: Pure random, no patterns. Humans tend to play paper more often, but this bot is statistically uniform.

faq.q: Can multiple people play at once?
faq.a: Currently 1-on-1 only. For groups, each plays the computer separately, or use the random name picker.
Against a random bot, any strategy averages 1/3 win rate. Against people, reading their patterns is key.

korea-holidays.description: See US federal holidays for this and next year at a glance. Includes floating holidays like Thanksgiving and Memorial Day, computed automatically.
korea-holidays.metaDescription: Free US federal holidays calendar. New Year's, MLK, Presidents' Day, Memorial Day, Juneteenth, July 4th, Labor Day, Thanksgiving, Christmas.

faq.a: No — this tool lists federal holidays only. States observe their own additional holidays (e.g., Cesar Chavez Day in California, Patriots' Day in Massachusetts).

faq.q: Why does Memorial Day move each year?
faq.a: Several US federal holidays are tied to a weekday rather than a date. Memorial Day is the last Monday of May; Thanksgiving is the fourth Thursday of November. The tool computes these automatically.

faq.q: What if a holiday falls on a weekend?
faq.a: Federally observed holidays usually shift to the nearest weekday (Friday if Saturday, Monday if Sunday). The tool shows the actual date; observance may differ at your employer.
Yes — Juneteenth (June 19) became a federal holiday in 2021. It commemorates the end of slavery in the United States.

faq.q: Can I see how many consecutive days off?
faq.a: The tool auto-highlights long weekends (3+ consecutive days). Useful for planning vacations.

faq.q: Do I get extra pay for working on a holiday?
faq.a: Federal law does not require holiday premium pay for private-sector workers. Most companies offer 1.5x or compensatory time off as a benefit; check your employer's policy.

lunch-picker.description: Use the roulette when you can't decide. Preloaded Korean/Chinese/Japanese/Western categories, or add your own menus.
lunch-picker.metaDescription: Free lunch roulette. Korean/Chinese/Japanese/Western, add your own menus.
howTo: Pick a category or add menu items yourself.
Spin again if you don't like the result.

faq.q: Do I have to follow the result?
faq.a: Just for fun. What your coworkers agree on matters more.
Korean (kimchi stew, samgyeopsal, bibimbap, gukbap), Chinese (jjajangmyeon, jjamppong, sweet & sour pork), Japanese (sushi, ramen, tonkatsu), Western (pasta, pizza, steak) and other common dishes.

faq.q: Can I add my own menu items?
faq.a: Yes. Add your usual restaurants or neighborhood favorites to make it more practical.

faq.q: What if I don't like the result?
faq.a: Spin again, or pick what you actually want. The roulette is a decision aid, not a binding choice.

faq.q: Can I make a diet-only roulette?
faq.a: Just enter diet menus like salad, grilled salmon, or chicken breast for your own diet-focused roulette.

baseball-stats.description: Calculate pitcher ERA, hitter batting average, OBP, SLG, and OPS instantly. For amateur baseball and watching games.
baseball-stats.metaDescription: Free baseball ERA/AVG/OPS. KBO and MLB compatible.
howTo: Enter the inputs (earned runs, innings, hits, at-bats).

faq.a: On-Base Percentage (OBP) + Slugging Percentage (SLG). A combined hitter metric: 0.800+ is good, 0.900+ is elite.
(Earned Runs × 9) ÷ Innings. Below 2.50 is ace-level, 4.00~4.50 is league average, 5.00+ is poor.
AVG is hits/at-bats. OBP is (hits+walks+HBP)/(at-bats+walks+HBP+sac flies). OBP is a more complete stat.
(singles×1 + doubles×2 + triples×3 + HR×4) ÷ at-bats. 0.500 is good, 0.600+ is slugger territory.
WAR (Wins Above Replacement) is too complex for this tool. Check official KBO/MLB stat sites.

faq.q: Same formulas for KBO and MLB?
faq.a: Core stats (AVG, ERA, OPS) are identical. League averages differ, so the same number can mean different things.

book-reading-time.description: Estimate how long it'll take to finish a book based on total pages and your reading speed. Uses average Korean reading speed.
book-reading-time.metaDescription: Free book reading time estimate. Pages × speed = finish time.
howTo: Adjust your reading speed (chars per minute or pages per minute).

faq.a: Korean average is 250~350 chars/min (about 2~3 minutes per page). English averages 200~300 words/min.

faq.q: How do I find my reading speed?
faq.a: Time yourself reading a familiar page. That gives you your average minutes per page.

faq.q: What about technical or hard books?
faq.a: Set speed to less than half of average. You may re-read paragraphs multiple times.
Audiobooks are usually 1.0~1.5x speed and 30~50% slower than reading. Needs separate calculation.

faq.q: How do I calc time left in a partially read book?
faq.a: Enter (total - read) pages instead of total.
About 7~8 books per year per adult by Korean census data. Consistency at your own pace matters most.

image-invert.description: Invert image colors to create a negative effect. Recreate old film photos, prepare images for dark mode, invert black-and-white diagrams, or experiment with design concepts.
image-invert.metaDescription: Free image color invert. Negative effect, instant conversion.

faq.a: Transparency is preserved; only colors invert. PNG transparent backgrounds remain transparent.

faq.q: What if the image is black and white?
faq.a: Black → white, white → black. Often used for dark-mode versions.

faq.q: How do I revert to the original?
faq.a: Apply invert once more to the inverted result. It's mathematically reversible.
This tool is image-only. For PDF, convert to images first, invert, then back to PDF.
Simple inversion can look awkward. Real dark-mode design usually requires redesigning palettes.

image-watermark-img.description: Overlay a logo or image as a watermark on a photo. Adjustable position, opacity, and size. Useful for photographer copyright marks, preventing image theft on blogs/SNS, company logos, and source credit on lecture materials.
image-watermark-img.metaDescription: Free image watermark. Logo overlay, adjustable position and opacity.

faq.a: 9 preset positions plus fine-tuning. Bottom-right is most common and least likely to obstruct content.
Yes. PNGs with transparent backgrounds blend naturally. White-background logos can show a visible rectangle.
30~50% looks good. Too dark obscures content; too light is barely a watermark.

faq.q: My watermark is getting cut off.
faq.a: It's likely too large or placed too close to the edge. Adjust size and position.

faq.q: Can I batch-apply to multiple images?
faq.a: Currently one at a time. Apply the same settings sequentially for multiple photos.

faq.q: What if I want a text watermark?
faq.a: Use the [Add Text to Image] tool — supports text, outline, and positioning.

image-color-transparent.description: Make a specific color (usually white background) transparent in an image. Useful for removing white backgrounds from logos, cleaning up signature/stamp scans, extracting icons, or making transparent images for slides.
image-color-transparent.metaDescription: Free image background transparency. PNG transparency, solid background removal.
howTo: Pick the color to make transparent.

faq.q: Does it work on complex backgrounds?
faq.a: Best for solid color backgrounds. AI background-removal tools are better for gradients or natural photos.
How close a pixel's color must be to the picked color to become transparent. Pick white with tolerance 30, and light grays also vanish. Too high and your content disappears.
No. JPG doesn't support transparency. Save as PNG.

faq.q: Can I make scanned signatures transparent?
faq.a: Yes. White-background scans clean up nicely with this tool. Then overlay on other images using [Image Watermark].

faq.q: Can I remove just the background behind a person?
faq.a: Hard with this tool. Use AI background removal services like remove.bg.

faq.q: Can I remove multiple colors at once?
faq.a: One color per pass. Re-upload the result to remove another color cumulatively.

image-channels.description: Separate an image's red, green, and blue channels into grayscale images. Useful for photo compositing, color analysis, digital forensics, print separation preview, and design learning.
image-channels.metaDescription: Free RGB channel separation. View red, green, blue channels independently.
howTo: Each channel (R, G, B) displays automatically.

faq.a: (1) Boost specific channels for compositing/editing, (2) diagnose camera sensor issues, (3) learn how digital images work.
Each channel has only intensity (no hue), so it's grayscale. White = 100% of that color, black = 0%.

faq.q: Which channel is brightest for red objects?
faq.a: The red channel — green and blue are dark. A way to visualize color physics.
This tool only supports RGB. CMYK is for print and needs a separate tool.
This tool only separates. Recombining needs Photoshop or GIMP's channel mixer.

faq.q: Good way to learn photo theory?
faq.a: Looking at RGB channels separately makes light synthesis and digital color easier to grasp.

image-free-rotate.description: Rotate images freely in 1° increments. Useful for straightening crooked photos. Great for fixing tilted phone shots, straightening skewed document scans, design effects, and rotated business card or invitation designs.
image-free-rotate.metaDescription: Free 1° image rotation. Fine angle, horizon correction.
howTo: Pick a fill color for the margins.

faq.a: Filled with your chosen color or transparency. Transparency only works with PNG output.
Right-angle (90, 180, 270) is faster via [Image Rotate]. Free angles use this tool.
Free-angle rotation interpolates pixels, causing slight blur. Right-angle is lossless; free-angle has tiny loss.
Usually -1 to 3° aligns the horizon. Use the fine-tune slider.

faq.q: How do I crop the corners after rotating?
faq.a: Download the result, then use [Image Crop]. Or use the auto-crop option if available.
One at a time currently. If all photos tilt the same way, apply the same setting sequentially.

html-to-text.description: Strip all tags from HTML and extract body text only. Useful for cleaning up email HTML bodies, copying website text, tidying RSS feeds, pasting cleanly into ChatGPT, and search-friendly text extraction.
html-to-text.metaDescription: Free HTML tag stripper. Webpage body extraction, email cleanup.

faq.a: Content inside <script> and <style> tags is excluded from the body.

automatically convert to line breaks.
Convert HTML emails to plain text for clean copying to notepad/documents. Image positions get replaced with alt text.
Plain text loses the grid; only cell content remains. For tables, use [HTML → Markdown] instead.

faq.q: Do emojis and special characters survive?
faq.a: Yes. UTF-8 text is preserved as-is.
This tool only converts HTML to text — it never executes anything. Safe to use.

html-to-markdown.description: Convert HTML to markdown. Useful for blog migrations (WordPress, Tistory, Naver Blog → GitHub, Notion), wiki conversions, moving notes to Obsidian, and cleaning email bodies.
html-to-markdown.metaDescription: Free HTML to markdown. turndown-based conversion.

faq.a: GFM (GitHub Flavored Markdown) extension handles tables. Complex tables (merged cells) get simplified.
turndown is the de facto standard for HTML → markdown conversion. Clean, reliable output.
Converted exactly to **bold**, *italic*, `code`.
→ ![alt](url), → [text](url).
(1) Export source HTML → (2) convert to markdown here → (3) import into Notion, Obsidian, Hexo, or Hugo.
<script>, <style>, <iframe>, and other non-content tags get removed.

markdown-to-text.description: Strip markdown syntax (**bold**, [link], # heading, etc.) and leave only the text. Useful for accurate character counts in cover letters or blog posts, sending markdown notes via plain email/KakaoTalk, and clean ChatGPT input.
markdown-to-text.metaDescription: Free markdown to text. Strip syntax, plain output.

faq.a: [text](url) → 'text'. The URL is removed (option to keep it available).
Asterisks and underscores are stripped; only the text remains.
`code` backticks are removed; content stays. Line breaks inside code blocks are preserved.

faq.q: Why is this good for character counting?
faq.a: Counting markdown symbols (#, *, []) inflates the count. Convert to plain text first, then use [Character Count] for accuracy.
![alt](url) → just the alt text. Since images don't display in plain text, alt becomes the content.
Markdown table grids are removed; cell content stays as plain text.

text-compress.description: Compress long text (JSON, code) with LZ-string into short strings. Useful for passing data via URL parameters, creating short shareable links, saving localStorage space, and sharing long code in chats.
text-compress.metaDescription: Free text compression. LZ-string, URL-safe encoding.
howTo: Enter the original text or compressed string.

faq.a: Repetitive text like JSON or code shrinks 70%+. Natural language shrinks 30~50%.
A common text compression library in JavaScript. Its URL-safe mode outputs strings that fit directly into URLs.
Base64 grows length 33% (encoding only); LZ-string compresses. For shorter output, use LZ-string.
URL-safe mode avoids special characters like ? = & — fully URL-safe.
No, it's compression not encryption — anyone can decompress. For length saving, not security.
Yes. Unicode is handled directly. Korean-heavy text typically compresses slightly less than English.

text-blockquote.description: Prepend '>' to text in markdown blockquote or email quote format. Useful for inserting quotes in markdown blog posts, quoting originals in email replies, making Slack/Discord blocks, and writing debate or rebuttal posts.
text-blockquote.metaDescription: Free blockquote/quote. Markdown and email format.
howTo: Copy the result into your blog or email.

faq.a: Depth 2 uses '>>', depth 3 uses '>>>', and so on. Useful for replies-to-replies in email.
Each line starts with '> '. Multi-paragraph quotes need '>' on every line — this tool handles it in one pass.

faq.q: Why is it used in email?
faq.a: Old-school email replies prefix the original with '>'. Plain-text email still follows this convention.
For code, code blocks (```) work better than quotes. In chats, combining quote and code helps readability.
Academic convention uses '[...]' or '…' for omissions. This tool only converts; ellipses are manual.

data-size.description: Convert between bytes, kilobytes, megabytes, gigabytes, terabytes, and petabytes. Both SI (1000) and IEC (1024) supported. Useful for disk capacity comparisons, bandwidth calculations, file size estimates, and cloud cost projections.
data-size.metaDescription: Free data size converter. B KB MB GB TB, both SI and IEC.

faq.a: KB (kilobyte, SI) = 1000 B; KiB (kibibyte, IEC) = 1024 B. Hard drives use SI; RAM and OS often use IEC.
Manufacturers use SI (1TB = 10¹²B); Windows uses IEC (1024-based) for display, making it look smaller. Both are correct.
MB (megabyte, capital B) = 8 Mb (megabit, lowercase b). Internet speeds (100Mbps) are bits; file sizes are bytes.

faq.q: Which convention is used in Korea?
faq.a: Legally SI (1KB=1000B), but computer fields often use IEC (1024-based). Mixed usage is common.
Google Drive uses SI (GB); Windows Explorer uses IEC (GiB). The same file can display different numbers.
Yes: PB (peta) → EB (exa) → ZB (zetta) → YB (yotta), all supported.

mime-types.description: Search by file extension or MIME type, both directions. Useful for HTTP response header configuration, file upload validation, security policy writing, email attachment handling, and web server config.
mime-types.metaDescription: Free MIME types reference. Extension ↔ Content-Type, both ways.
howTo: Search by extension or MIME type.
Copy results into your code or config.

faq.a: 100+ common extensions. Images, video, audio, documents, code, and archives.
Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions — a standard identifier for file format (e.g., image/png, application/json). Used in HTTP and email standards.
Wrong MIME can cause (1) browsers to mishandle files, (2) security bypass risks, (3) broken downloads or display.

faq.q: How do I detect spoofed extensions?
faq.a: Don't trust the extension — also check the magic number (first bytes). Use the file-type library.
If non-standard, use application/x-yourname. Standard formats are preferred for compatibility.

css-colors.description: All 148 CSS named colors with their HEX codes, searchable. Useful for color inspiration while writing CSS, rapid prototyping, and writing design guides.
css-colors.metaDescription: Free CSS color names reference. 148 standard colors, click to copy.
howTo: Search by color name or HEX.

faq.a: CSS Color Module Level 4. Includes both basic (16) and extended (148) named colors.
Both are standard with identical results. 'red' and '#ff0000' are the same. Names for readability; HEX for precision.
Added to honor Eric Meyer's daughter Rebecca. Officially in the CSS spec.

faq.q: How do I pick from similar colors?
faq.a: Similar names differ subtly — e.g., lightgray(#D3D3D3) vs silver(#C0C0C0). Stick to one palette for design consistency.
Tailwind has its own palette (red-50 to red-900). CSS named colors are universal but lack the gradation needed for full design systems.

http-methods.description: Summary of HTTP method meanings, usage, and idempotency. Useful for RESTful API design, backend learning, interview prep, and API documentation.
http-methods.metaDescription: Free HTTP methods reference. GET POST PUT DELETE PATCH meaning and idempotency.
howTo: Click a method to see details.
Check usage examples and idempotency info.

faq.a: Multiple executions produce the same server state. GET, PUT, DELETE are idempotent; POST is not. Repeating a POST creates multiple resources.
PUT replaces the whole resource; PATCH applies partial updates. PUT is idempotent; PATCH may or may not be.
If the client picks the resource ID, use PUT. If the server picks it, use POST. A common point of confusion in REST design.
204 No Content is common per standard. Some APIs return the deleted resource with a 200.
Auto-used in CORS preflight. Rarely called directly but useful for discovering allowed methods.

env-parser.description: Convert environment variable files to JSON objects, or convert JSON back to .env format. Useful for debugging environment settings, migrating variables across systems, and validating CI/CD environment variables.
env-parser.metaDescription: Free .env parser. KEY=VALUE → JSON, both directions.

faq.a: Both single and double quotes work. 'value with spaces' parses correctly.
Comments are removed when converting to JSON, and not regenerated when going back to .env.
Standard .env supports single-line only. Use \n escapes or base64 encoding for multi-line values.
All processing happens in the browser and never leaves. Still, avoid pasting real production .env files into public tools.
(1) Embed directly in code, (2) intermediate step to other formats (.toml, .yaml), (3) key-value structure validation.

jamo-decompose.description: Decompose Hangul syllables into initial/medial/final jamo, or compose them back. Useful for Korean search and autocomplete, IME conversion, phonological analysis, and learning to code Korean text.
jamo-decompose.metaDescription: Free Hangul jamo decomposition. Initial/medial/final, double-final support.
howTo: Enter a syllable to decompose into jamo.

faq.a: ㄳ, ㄵ, ㄶ, ㄺ, ㄻ, ㄼ, ㄽ, ㄾ, ㄿ, ㅀ, ㅄ — all decompose and recompose correctly.
(1) Initial-consonant search ('ㅎㄱ' → '한국'), (2) IME conversion, (3) Korean phonology algorithms. Essential for Korean apps and search.
Uses Unicode Hangul Jamo (U+1100~U+11FF), not the compatibility jamo (U+3131~U+318F).
By default they're one unit. An option further decomposes them to ㅗ+ㅏ.
Decompose each character → extract initials → match user input. '한국' → 'ㅎㄱ', '한식' → 'ㅎㅅ'.
Each character takes microseconds. Tens of thousands of characters process instantly.

duration-format.description: Convert numeric seconds (7200) to readable formats (2:00:00 or 2 hours) and back. Useful for video/music durations, log analysis, API response handling, and workout records.
duration-format.metaDescription: Free seconds to time. h:m:s, natural language, ISO 8601.
howTo: Enter seconds or a time format.

faq.a: Yes — PT1H30M (1h 30m), PT45S (45s). Common in YouTube API and ISO standard responses.
(1) 7200 sec, (2) 02:00:00, (3) 2 hours, (4) 2h 0m 0s, (5) PT2H. All shown simultaneously.
Defaults to positive. Negative durations are uncommon and may need separate handling.
Yes. Even 10,000 hours (1.14 years) converts cleanly.
Optional ms unit supported. Useful for game frames and web performance metrics.
YouTube Data API for video length, JSON Schema durations, some calendar APIs.

bcrypt-hash.description: Generate and verify bcrypt hashes with adjustable cost factor. Useful for auth system development, test dummy data, and database checks.
bcrypt-hash.metaDescription: Free bcrypt hash. Password hashing, adjustable cost factor.
howTo: Generate or verify against an existing hash.

faq.q: Can I use this in production?
faq.a: For testing and learning. In production, use bcryptjs/bcrypt on the server. Pasting passwords into external tools isn't recommended.
Hash iteration count (2^cost). Higher is safer but slower. 10 (2024 standard), 12 (high security), 14+ (very secure but very slow).
SHA-256 is a fast hash (for verification); bcrypt is slow (for password protection). Slow hashes resist brute-force attacks.
bcrypt auto-embeds the salt in the hash. No separate handling. The hash itself has $2b$10$... including the salt.
Argon2 is newer with strong memory-attack resistance. bcrypt is more battle-tested and widely compatible. For new projects, Argon2 is recommended.

faq.q: Same hash if I hash the same password twice?
faq.a: No. The salt differs each time, so the hash differs. Verification compares password + hash.

rot-all.description: Display results for ROT1–25 all at once. Useful for Caesar cipher brute-force decoding in CTFs, quickly finding the right shift when unknown, and cipher learning.
rot-all.metaDescription: Free ROT all variants. 1~25 at once, CTF Caesar cipher decoding.

faq.a: Yes. Half of 26 letters, so applying it twice restores the original. Most popular shift.
[Caesar Cipher] applies a single shift; this tool shows all shifts at once for solving puzzles or CTFs.
26 equals the original (no change). 1~25 covers every distinct result.
Currently you scan the results yourself for English or Korean words. Some advanced tools auto-detect.

faq.q: Does ROT47 have an all-variants version?
faq.a: ROT47 is wider in scope; this tool focuses on alphabet ROT.

card-mask.description: Auto-detect and asterisk-mask card numbers, Korean Resident Registration Numbers, phone numbers, and emails. Useful for pre-share log checks, screenshot prep, hiding personal info in blog posts and presentations, and pre-analysis anonymization.
card-mask.metaDescription: Free sensitive data masking. Cards/RRN/phone/email auto-detection.

faq.a: Korean credit cards (16 digits), Korean RRN (13 digits), mobile and landline phones (10~11 digits), and emails.
Example: 010-1234-5678 → 010-****-5678, or 940101-1******** format. Some digits remain to prevent re-identification.
Long digit sequences may be mistaken for cards. Always review the output before using.

faq.q: Does it work for foreign cards/phones?
faq.a: Korean-focused. Foreign cards (15, 19 digits) and international phone formats are only partially detected.
Technical masking is step one. Compliance also needs data policies, access control, and encryption.
Masking is irreversible. Keep the original safely.

pdf-images-extract.description: Render each PDF page as a high-resolution PNG and save as a ZIP bundle. Useful for using PDF in slide decks, capturing lecture materials, sharing PDF content on blogs/SNS, and making card news.
pdf-images-extract.metaDescription: Free PDF image extraction. High-res PNG, batch ZIP download.
howTo: Press extract to convert each page to PNG.

faq.a: Currently it renders pages as PNG. Extracting just embedded JPG/PNG images requires a different tool.
Nearly the same. This tool focuses on high-res batch ZIP; [PDF → Image] has more format and resolution flexibility.
Pull the page from the ZIP. Or use [Extract PDF Pages] to get one page first, then convert.

faq.q: Does it work on scanned PDFs?
faq.a: Yes — scans render as PNG too, preserving the scan quality.

faq.q: How do I save as JPG?
faq.a: Default is PNG. Download and use [PNG → JPG] for batch conversion.

pdf-n-up.description: Combine multiple pages into one page in 2x2 or 2x1 layouts for printable booklets and summaries. Saves paper, prints 4-page-per-sheet lecture notes, and makes presentation handouts.
pdf-n-up.metaDescription: Free PDF N-up. 2up·4up·8up multiple pages per sheet, print saver.

faq.a: Default margins apply so prints don't get cut at the edges.
2up is half size; 4up is 1/4. PDFs with 12pt+ body text usually work fine at 4up. Stick to 2up for smaller text.
This tool is plain N-up only. For booklets (auto-ordered saddle-stitch), use a dedicated booklet tool or your printer driver.
Yes. Export slides as PDF, then use 4up/6up/9up for printable distribution.

pdf-page-size.description: Change all pages to A4, Letter, Legal, B5, or other sizes. Useful for converting US Letter PDFs to Korean A4, switching to B5 for booklets. Aspect-preserving mode avoids content clipping.
pdf-page-size.metaDescription: Free PDF page size change. A4 Letter Legal B5, aspect-preserving.

faq.a: Default mode preserves aspect (fit), so nothing clips. If pages are larger than the target, they shrink with margins; smaller, and margins are added.
Letter is US standard (216×279mm); A4 is Korean/EU standard (210×297mm). Letter is slightly wider and shorter.

faq.q: Will a printed PDF look good after resizing?
faq.a: Shrinking is usually clean. Enlarging may lose quality — re-export from the source if possible.
Currently all pages get the same size. Use split/convert/merge for per-page sizes.
Common ISO sizes (A and B series) and US Letter/Legal are supported. For unusual sizes, use [PDF Page Crop] or other tools.

video-resize.description: Convert videos to 360p, 720p, 1080p, or 4K. Useful for reducing 4K to 720p for KakaoTalk attachments, making mobile-friendly versions, and shrinking lecture videos for data savings.

faq.a: Yes — original ratio is kept by default, scaling one dimension. 16:9 stays 16:9 after conversion.
YouTube 1080p, KakaoTalk/Instagram 720p, data-saver videos 480p, mobile preview 360p. 4K is for large screens or editing sources.
No. Going higher than the original just blurs pixels. Don't upscale beyond source. For real upscaling, you need AI tools.
1080p → 720p typically cuts size by half or more. For aggressive reduction, chain with [Video Compress].
Audio tracks are kept unchanged.
Re-encoding takes 1~2x the video length. Downsizing 4K to 720p takes longer due to more pixels.

audio-merge.description: Join multiple audio files in order into one. Useful for combining multi-session lecture recordings, music medleys, podcast intro/main/outro bundles, and split meeting recordings.
audio-merge.metaDescription: Free audio merge. Multiple MP3·WAV into one, reorderable.

faq.a: Same format and bitrate is recommended. Mixed formats auto-convert but may lose quality or take longer.
Currently concat only. For silence gaps, insert empty MP3s or use a dedicated audio editor.
Only sequential concat for now. Layering BGM and voice needs Audacity or another mixer.
No. Big volume differences sound off. Use [Audio Volume] beforehand to match dB levels.
Usually same as input. MP3 in, MP3 out; WAV in, WAV out.

audio-volume.description: Boost or lower audio in decibel (dB) units. Useful for raising too-quiet lecture recordings, lowering loud mic input, and matching volume across multiple audio files.
audio-volume.metaDescription: Free audio volume adjust. dB increase/decrease, clipping warning, MP3/WAV.
howTo: Enter dB adjustment (positive: boost, negative: cut).

faq.q: How loud can I go without distortion?
faq.a: Above +6dB risks clipping (distortion). +3dB is generally safe.
Decibel — a volume unit. +6dB ≈ double the volume; -6dB ≈ half. Quiet lecture audio often improves with +3~6dB.

faq.q: Can I match volume across files?
faq.a: Currently one file at a time. Automated 'normalize' across multiple files isn't built in — adjust each manually.
If a normalize option is offered, it sets the peak near 0dB. For precise loudness (LUFS), use a pro editor.
Lossless formats (WAV, FLAC) stay intact. Lossy formats (MP3) re-encode with minor loss.

exchange-rate.description: Enter the rate manually and convert KRW to various currencies or vice versa. Useful for travel budgeting, overseas shopping conversions, and foreign remittance amounts.
exchange-rate.metaDescription: Free exchange rate calculator. KRW/USD/JPY/EUR conversion, manual rate entry.
howTo: Check the rate on Naver/Daum/bank sites.
Enter KRW or foreign amount to auto-convert.

faq.a: Operates offline with no external API dependency. Check rates on Naver Finance, Daum Finance, or your bank, then enter manually.

faq.q: Which rate should I use for travel exchange?
faq.a: Banks charge fees on top of the base rate. About 1.5% for cash, 1% for remittance. Better with exchange preferential rates.

faq.q: Which rate for direct overseas purchases?
faq.a: Credit cards add about 0.5% on top of the base rate. PayPal uses its own (less favorable) rate.
Base rate + ATM fees (usually 3000~5000 KRW). Can be costlier than direct exchange.
One currency at a time. Switch rates to compare multiple currencies.
10%+ swings over a year are common. Timing matters for large remittance or exchange.

statistics.description: Enter a list of numbers to get mean, median, mode, standard deviation, variance, quartiles (Q1, Q3), range, and sum in one go. Useful for homework and papers, test score analysis, survey results, and experiment data.
howTo: Enter numbers separated by commas, line breaks, or spaces.

faq.a: Both shown. Sample stdev divides by n-1; population stdev divides by n. For sample data, use sample statistics.
Copying an Excel column gives line-break-separated data. Paste directly.

faq.q: When is median better than mean?
faq.a: When outliers exist. E.g., one billionaire skews salary averages but doesn't affect the median.
How spread out the data is from the mean. Small = clustered near mean; large = widely scattered.
Quartiles divide data into 4 parts. Q1 = lower 25%, Q3 = upper 25%. Used in box plots.
Only basic statistics — no inferential stats like t-tests or normality tests. Use SPSS, R, or Python for those.

car-fuel.description: Calculate driving cost from fuel efficiency (km/L) and gas price. Useful for monthly commute fuel cost, trip fuel estimates, car model comparisons (savings from better mileage), and carpool cost splitting.
car-fuel.metaDescription: Free car fuel calculator. Gas cost, commute cost, trip cost.

faq.a: Currently gas/diesel only. EVs need kWh/100km and electricity rate (kWh) for separate calculation.

faq.q: How do I find my fuel efficiency?
faq.a: Official spec is in the owner's manual. The trip computer shows real-world figures. City vs highway differs a lot.
City usually 70~80% of highway. Stops and acceleration hurt efficiency.

faq.q: I don't match official MPG. Why?
faq.a: Official figures are lab-measured. Real driving is 10~20% lower typically. Driving style, road, and weather matter.
(1) Avoid hard acceleration and braking, (2) keep tires properly inflated, (3) reduce cargo, (4) steady highway speed below 100km/h.
Compare price/L × efficiency. Diesel has cheaper fuel but may have higher car/maintenance costs.

rent-calc.description: Convert jeonse deposits to monthly rent and back using the conversion rate. Useful for comparing upfront deposit costs when moving, evaluating jeonse vs monthly rent options, and partial deposit + monthly hybrid plans.
rent-calc.metaDescription: Free jeonse/monthly rent converter. Deposit, monthly rent, both ways.
howTo: Enter jeonse amount, or deposit + monthly rent.

faq.a: Annual % used to convert deposit to monthly rent. Deposit × rate ÷ 12 = monthly rent. Korean average is 3~6%/year, varies by region and property.
Under Korea's Housing Lease Protection Act, base rate + 2% (about 5.5% in 2024) is the cap. Landlords can't unilaterally raise it more.

faq.q: Convert 100M KRW deposit + 500K monthly rent to jeonse?
faq.a: At 5% rate, 500K monthly = ~120M deposit equivalent. Total ≈ 220M jeonse.
If you can afford the deposit and want stability, jeonse. If liquidity matters, monthly. Don't decide on conversion alone — check your finances.
Banjeonse = deposit + rent. Use the tool to lower deposit while raising rent or vice versa.
Only rent conversion. Add management/utility fees separately to your budget.

sleep-recommend.description: Find optimal wake or bed times based on 90-minute sleep cycles. Useful for deciding nap length after a late shift, optimal bedtime before a morning exam or interview, and jet lag planning.
sleep-recommend.metaDescription: Free sleep time recommend. 90-min cycles, refreshed wake time.
howTo: Enter your target wake or bedtime.

faq.a: One sleep cycle (REM-NREM) averages 90 minutes. Waking mid-cycle feels tired; waking at cycle end feels refreshed.
Individual cycles range 80~110 minutes. 90 is an average; could be off by ±15 minutes.

faq.q: How many hours should I sleep?
faq.a: Adults need 7~9 hours (4~6 cycles). 4 cycles (6h) is minimum; 5 cycles (7.5h) is recommended.
Usually 10~20 minutes assumed. The tool adds this automatically.
Naps are best at 20~30 min (light recovery) or 90 min (one full cycle). 60-min naps wake you mid-deep-sleep, often leaving you groggier.
Yes. Beyond duration, dark environment, consistent timing, and reducing caffeine also matter for sleep hygiene.

blood-donation.description: Calculate the next eligible donation date based on Korean Red Cross standards using your last donation date and type. Useful for regular donor scheduling, blood donation certificate collection plans, group donation events, and multi-type donation intervals.
blood-donation.metaDescription: Free blood donation date calculator. Whole blood/plasma/platelets, Korean Red Cross standards.
howTo: Pick your last donation date and type.

faq.a: Whole blood 8 weeks (56 days); plasma 2 weeks (14 days); platelets 2 weeks. Korean Red Cross standard.
Whole blood draws all blood; apheresis takes only plasma or platelets and returns the rest. Faster recovery means more frequent donation.

faq.q: How long to rest after donating?
faq.a: 15~30 min immediately after; avoid strenuous exercise and alcohol that day. Normal activity in 2~3 hours.
Age 16~69, weight 50kg (men) / 45kg (women) or more, 8+ weeks since last donation. Some medications, travel history, or colds may disqualify temporarily.

faq.q: What are donation certificates used for?
faq.a: Transfer to family or friends in need, or use yourself for partial medical cost reduction if you need a transfusion.
One whole blood donation recovers in about 8 weeks. The Red Cross checks hemoglobin before each donation to confirm safety.

installment.description: Calculate monthly payment and total fees from principal, rate, and term. Useful for checking affordability before big purchases (appliances, furniture, travel), comparing interest-free installments vs lump sum, and comparing fees across cards.
installment.metaDescription: Free installment calculator. Card monthly payment, total fees.
howTo: Enter principal, interest rate (annual %), and term (months).
Monthly payment and total fees appear.

faq.q: How do I find my card's interest rate?
faq.a: Check the card company's website or call them. Usually 15~20% annual, varying by card and tier.
0% fee. List price split evenly. Available periods (2/3/6 months) vary by card and merchant.
Installments with fees cost more overall. But you may pick them for (1) cash flow distribution, (2) card benefits (installment-only points).
Varies by card. Usually unaccrued fees are refunded, but some charge prepayment penalties. Check the card terms.
Toss, KakaoPay, Payco each have their own fee structures separate from card companies. Check their terms and rates.
Paying on time has no effect or is slightly positive. Late payments immediately hurt your credit score.

korean-phone.description: Normalize phone numbers of any format to a clean US standard like (XXX) XXX-XXXX. Useful for cleaning up Excel/CRM/contact data, handling area codes, and converting to international +1 format.
korean-phone.metaDescription: Free US phone number formatter. (XXX) XXX-XXXX, +1 international, Excel batch cleanup.
howTo: Enter one number or multiple numbers on separate lines.
Each is normalized to the standard format automatically.
Copy the cleaned results into Excel or your database.

faq.a: Yes. It converts between +1 XXX-XXX-XXXX and the national (XXX) XXX-XXXX format both ways.
Yes. 3-digit US area codes are detected and formatted correctly.
Yes — digits, spaces, dashes, dots, and parentheses are all cleaned up automatically.

faq.q: Can I process many numbers at once?
faq.a: Yes. Enter multiple numbers separated by line breaks and they are all normalized.
Numbers that do not match the standard 10-digit US length are flagged with a warning.
All processing happens in your browser. Nothing is uploaded.

korean-biz-num.description: Validate the checksum of Korea's 10-digit business registration number. Useful for verifying counterparty info, checking before issuing tax invoices, B2B system data integrity, and first-pass risk checks.
korean-biz-num.metaDescription: Free Korean business number validator. Checksum check, format verification.

faq.q: Does it verify the business exists?
faq.a: No. This tool only checks checksum format. Confirm actual registration on Hometax's 'Business Registration Status Inquiry'.
The last digit of the 10 is computed from the first 9 using a fixed rule. Random inputs almost never pass.
XXX-XX-XXXXX. First 3 = issuing tax office; next 2 = entity type (individual/corporate); last 5 = serial + checksum.
Yes — corporate registration is 13 digits, for corporations only. Business numbers belong to all businesses (individual or corporate).

faq.q: Safe to validate my own number?
faq.a: All processing happens in the browser — nothing leaves.
Currently one at a time. For bulk, use Excel formulas or a dedicated script.

korean-rrn.description: Validate the checksum of a 13-digit Korean Resident Registration Number and extract birth date, gender, and foreigner status. All processing stays in-browser for safety. Useful for form validation, auto-fill UI prototyping, and quickly checking your own RRN digits.
korean-rrn.metaDescription: Free Korean RRN validator. Checksum, birth date and gender extraction, browser-only.
howTo: Enter the 13-digit Korean Resident Registration Number.
Checksum validity, birth date, and gender display.

faq.a: All processing happens in-browser and never transmits to any server. Verify in the Network tab if you like.
YYMMDD-SXXXXXC. First 6 = birth date; first of last 7 (S) = gender/nationality; next 4 = region/serial; last = checksum.
1, 3 (male, Korean); 2, 4 (female, Korean); 5, 7 (male, foreigner); 6, 8 (female, foreigner); 9 (male, born 1900s); 0 (female, born 1900s). 9/0 are fading out.
The last digit is computed from the first 12 by a fixed rule. Random 13-digit inputs almost never pass — useful for format validation.
This tool only validates format. Real registration status is only confirmable via Ministry of Interior / Government24 with proper authentication.
Same 13-digit structure, validated identically. Gender digit uses 5~8.

faq.q: Is it OK to expose my RRN?
faq.a: Absolutely not. This tool is for self-check or development verification only. RRN is the most sensitive personal info — exposure risks identity theft.

family-kinship.description: Enter paternal/maternal relations to see the exact degree of kinship and Korean honorifics (gomo, imo, dangsuk, etc.). Useful for sorting out tricky honorifics at holidays, preparing wedding/funeral greetings, and family tree writing.
family-kinship.metaDescription: Free Korean kinship calculator. Paternal/maternal, honorifics (gomo, dangsuk).
howTo: Pick family relation steps from your perspective.
The kinship degree and Korean honorific display.

faq.a: Currently only direct and collateral kin. In-law honorifics follow separate rules and aren't supported.
Direct line: 1 generation = 1 degree (parents-you = 1, grandparents-you = 2). Collateral: count steps through the common ancestor (parents-sibling = 2, sibling's child = 3). Father = 1, uncle = 3.
Yes. Father's brothers are baekbu/sukbu; mother's brothers are oesamchon. Father's sisters are gomo; mother's sisters are imo.
Cousins are children of your aunts and uncles. Add 'sachon' (cousin) to sibling/elder terms. Formally there are 'jaejong' etc., but daily speech just uses 'sachon'.

faq.q: Don't count beyond 8 degrees as relatives?
faq.a: Legal family scope is up to 8 degrees by blood and 4 by marriage. Beyond that, honorifics largely disappear.
Yes. Both traditional Chinese-character honorifics and modern common terms (like 'big dad') appear together.

number-format.description: Convert large numbers to formats like commas (1,000,000), Korean units (100만/1 million), underscores (1_000_000), or scientific (1.0e6). Useful for reports, data tables, readability, receipts, and invoices.
number-format.metaDescription: Free number format converter. Commas, Korean units, underscores, scientific.

faq.q: Does it handle very large numbers?
faq.a: Uses BigInt for unlimited digits. Even 100-digit numbers convert accurately.
1만 (10⁴), 1억 (10⁸), 1조 (10¹²), 1경 (10¹⁶), etc. Korean large-number notation, different from English (thousand/million/billion).
Programming languages (JavaScript, Python, etc.) support underscores in large numbers like 1_000_000 for readability. This tool converts quickly.
Very large or very small numbers (astronomy, physics, statistics). 1.5e6 = 1,500,000.
Yes — negatives (-1,000), decimals (1,234.56), negative exponents (1.5e-5) all supported.
Currently Korean Hangul units only. Chinese-character numerals need a separate tool.

stars.description: Convert scores to star (★) emoji and copy as text. Half-stars supported. Useful for blog reviews, SNS rating posts, email signatures, and presentation slides.
stars.metaDescription: Free star rating viz. 4.5/5 → ★★★★½ text, half-stars.

faq.a: Unicode stars display in KakaoTalk, Discord, Twitter, blogs, Tistory, email — anywhere. They're text, not images.
★★★★½ format with half-star (½) or ☆ empty-star options. Auto-selects the appropriate style by environment.
Yes. Set max to 10 and display 7.5/10. Star count auto-adjusts to the max.
Tools may let you pick alternates like hearts (♥) or diamonds (◆). Check the tool's options.
Unicode itself has no color, but HTML/Markdown can color them. Use your blog editor's color tools.
They look slightly different depending on system fonts (Apple, Windows, Google).

golf-handicap.description: Estimate USGA-style handicap from recent round scores. Useful for self-assessing skill, matching handicaps with partners, setting friendly round betting bases, and tracking seasonal skill changes.
golf-handicap.metaDescription: Free golf handicap. USGA-style, quick estimate.
howTo: Add course rating and slope if available.

faq.a: Official handicaps (GHIN, KGA) require association registration and verified rounds. This tool estimates for personal reference.
USGA standard: average of the best 8 of your last 20 rounds × 0.96 = handicap index.
A scratch golfer. Averages around par (72) per round. Top 1~2% of players.
About 18~22 — averages bogey pace.
Minimum 5, recommended 10~20. Fewer rounds get swung by single great/poor rounds.

faq.q: Do you just use raw scores (e.g., 92)?
faq.a: It uses the differential — score adjusted for course difficulty (rating, slope). The tool calculates automatically.

text-similarity.description: Calculate Levenshtein edit distance and percentage similarity between two strings. Useful for typo detection, similar-word lookup, search autocomplete, and data deduplication.
text-similarity.metaDescription: Free text similarity. Levenshtein edit distance, percentage.
howTo: Edit distance and similarity (%) display instantly.

faq.q: Is it fast for long documents?
faq.a: Up to thousands of characters processes instantly. Very long texts (tens of thousands+) take longer.
Minimum number of edits (insert, delete, replace) to transform one string into another. 'cat' → 'dog' takes 3 edits.
100% = identical; 0% = totally different. 80%+ generally means very similar; below 50% is different.
Yes. Calculations are syllable-level. For jamo-level comparison, pair with [Hangul Jamo Decomposition].
(1) Typo correction candidates, (2) DB duplicate row detection, (3) fuzzy search matching, (4) basic plagiarism checks.
Jaro-Winkler, cosine similarity, n-gram, etc., but Levenshtein is the most intuitive and common.

font-preview.description: Live preview how text looks in any font. Useful for CSS font decisions, website design mockups, Korean font comparisons, and choosing fonts for business cards or posters.
font-preview.metaDescription: Free font preview. System and web fonts, Korean support.
howTo: Adjust size, weight, and letter spacing too.

faq.a: Yes — add the Google Fonts URL. Common fonts like 'Roboto', 'Inter', 'Pretendard' are often pre-installed on systems.
Pretendard, Noto Sans KR, IBM Plex Sans KR, Nanum Gothic — all free with great readability.

faq.q: Can I see all my installed fonts?
faq.a: Browsers hide the font list for privacy. Type font names manually to preview.
D2Coding, Source Code Pro, JetBrains Mono, Fira Code, etc., for coding-style preview.
(1) Font isn't installed, (2) typo in name, (3) licensing issues. Check Computed in DevTools to see the actually-used font.
Your selected font may not support Korean glyphs. English fonts usually fall back to system Korean fonts.

word-cloud.description: Visualize frequently used words by size to make a word cloud. Useful for keyword visualization in presentations, summarizing survey responses, theme analysis of papers and blog posts, and mind map/infographic design.
word-cloud.metaDescription: Free word cloud. Korean and English text viz, PNG save.
howTo: Adjust stopword removal, colors, and shape.

faq.a: Yes — Korean, English, and emoji all supported, with Korean stopword removal (이/가/은/는, etc.).

faq.q: What kind of text works best?
faq.a: Text with clear, repeated keywords (surveys, papers, blogs, speeches). Too short lacks variety; too long becomes cluttered.

faq.q: Can I use the result in PPT?
faq.a: Save as PNG for slides, reports, or infographics. Use high-res save for print.

faq.q: Can I change colors and shape?
faq.a: Color palette and shape (square, circle, heart, etc.) are options. Customize for brand colors.
For frequency tables without visualization, use [Word Frequency Analysis].
Add your own stopwords to the list. Useful for removing company names or proper nouns.

random-string.description: Generate strings with cryptographically secure Web Crypto random. Useful for API keys, session tokens, temporary IDs and passwords, invitation codes, and UUID alternatives.
random-string.metaDescription: Free random string. API key/token, Web Crypto secure random.
howTo: Pick length and charset (alphabet, digits, symbols).
Press generate for a secure random string.

faq.q: Can I use this as a password?
faq.a: For passwords, use [Password Generator]. This tool is for general-purpose random like API keys and tokens.
The browser's cryptographically secure random API. Stronger than Math.random() statistically and security-wise.
UUID is a fixed 128-bit format; random strings let you choose length and charset. Random for short tokens/IDs; UUID for distributed system IDs.
Standard ASCII (alphabet, digits, symbols) only. Korean isn't typical for tokens/keys.
API keys 32 chars (~192 bits); session tokens 32~64 chars are common. Shorter increases collision risk.
Optional URL-safe charset (A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, _) is available.

emoji-search.description: Search emojis by Korean or English keyword and copy with one click. Useful for KakaoTalk/Instagram/Twitter posts, decorating Notion page headers, email signatures, GitHub README, and presentation highlights.
emoji-search.metaDescription: Free emoji search. Korean and English keywords, click to copy.

faq.a: Unicode 15+ standard emojis included. 2024 additions also covered.
Yes — Korean keywords like '웃음' (smile), '사랑' (love), '돈' (money), '동물' (animal) all work.

faq.q: Why doesn't my copied emoji show?
faq.a: If the recipient's device lacks the latest Unicode, it shows as a square. Common on older devices and some corporate messengers.
Over 3,790 emojis (Unicode 15.1), organized by category.
Person emojis offer 5 skin tones and gender options. Click to pick a variant.
Family and profession combos are searchable. Some devices split these into separate parts.

user-agent.description: Extract browser, OS, device, and version from User-Agent strings. Useful for web log analysis, compatibility debugging, analytics segmentation, and bot/crawler identification.
howTo: Paste a UA string or click 'My UA'.
Browser, OS, and device info display.

faq.a: The string a browser uses to introduce itself to servers. Goes in the HTTP User-Agent header, format like 'Mozilla/5.0 ...'.
Historical. In the 1990s, some sites only recognized Mozilla, so other browsers pretended to be Mozilla. Now it's standard.
Chrome is reducing UA info via 'User-Agent Client Hints'. UA will simplify, with detail moving to separate headers.
Keywords like iPhone, iPad, Android, Mobile help. Accurate detection needs viewport and touch events too.
Yes — DevTools and extensions can change UA. Don't use UA for security/identity.
Bots like Googlebot, Bingbot, Slackbot identify themselves in UA. Malicious bots may pretend to be human, though.

password-comparator.description: Evaluate two passwords side by side to see which is stronger. Useful for before/after comparison when changing passwords, showing family or colleagues why weak passwords are risky, and security education materials.
password-comparator.metaDescription: Free password compare. Entropy and pattern analysis.
howTo: Entropy, expected crack time, and weaknesses display side by side.

faq.a: Entropy (randomness), dictionary word matching, keyboard patterns, character repetition, and common-password databases combined.
Randomness measured in bits. 60+ bits is reasonably safe; 80+ is very safe. Increases with length and character diversity.

faq.q: Which of two passwords is better?
faq.a: Generally the longer one with more character types. Side-by-side makes it obvious.
No. Everything stays in your browser. Still, avoid pasting production passwords into external tools.
